payload.text: I read this as a full independent release-gate review - I’ll rerun gates 1–5 in order, inspect Rust code quality, write the evidence-backed review, and issue the verdict without changing features or `Sources/`.

I found a pre-existing dirty worktree, including many `Sources/` changes; I will not alter or revert them. The Swift cleanliness gate will therefore reflect the actual checkout state, while all runnable checks continue independently.

Gate 1 now passes after three mechanical warning-only cleanups: removing one redundant integer cast, deleting an unused local ScreenCapture permission declaration, and dropping an unused audio timestamp from the internal media event. No behavior or feature work was added.

Gates 2–4 pass: 105 Rust tests passed, VM interop emitted `INTEROP_PASS`, and the 200-frame release benchmark measured p50 3.05 ms and p99 5.01 ms. I’m proceeding with every Swift subcheck even though the required `Sources/` cleanliness predicate is already expected to fail from the pre-existing diff.

All executable checks are complete. The Swift binaries and XCTest suite pass, but gate 5 fails because `git diff --quiet -- Sources/` returned 1 with 30 tracked `Sources/` files changed; under the stated approval rule, the final verdict must be NOT APPROVED.
